reforms.description: Canada replaced its tax concession system for scientific research expenditures with a system of outright grants. Previously, firms could claim current research outlays as a business expense plus an additional 50% of the extent to which these exceeded 1961 research expenditures. The new grant system is expected to lead to further increases in research outlays.
reforms.package_name: 1965 Industrial Efficiency and Technological Standards Programme
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Replacing tax concessions with direct grants removes administrative complexity and is expected to stimulate private-sector R&D investment, raising innovation capacity and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states: 'The tax concessions previously in force regarding expenditures on scientific research... are to be replaced by a system of outright grants.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant shift in the design of R&D support instruments from indirect (tax concessions) to direct (grants), expected to increase research outlays. Narrower in scope than a system-wide overhaul but meaningful for private-sector innovation incentives.
reforms.source_quote: The tax concessions previously in force regarding expenditures on scientific research, under which a firm could claim not only its current research outlays as a business expense but also an additional 50 per cent of the extent to which these exceeded its research expenditures in 1961, are to be replaced by a system of outright grants.
